paragraphs: Baker, here's the big idea: Jesus tells His friends the hard news on the very night they're sorrowful, and He doesn't leave them alone with it. He says, "it is for your benefit that I am going away," because if He goes, He will send the Advocate (John 16:7). That means the Spirit of truth comes to guide them "into all truth" and to glorify Jesus (John 16:13-14). I bet that sounded backwards at that table, but I'll tell you what, God's help doesn't always look like what we'd order.

Now here's the part I love. Jesus doesn't pretend the sorrow isn't real. He says, "You will grieve, but your grief will turn to joy," and He compares it to a woman in childbirth who forgets her anguish because of her joy (John 16:20-21). Then He promises, "no one will take away your joy" (John 16:22). So when you're in a hard stretch, friend, the sorrow isn't the end of the story, and I think that's worth holding onto with your whole mustache, if you had one.

And then comes the honesty that gets me every time. Jesus knows the disciples will scatter and leave Him alone, yet He says, "I am not alone, because the Father is with Me" (John 16:32). He tells them this so that in Him they "may have peace," because "In the world you will have tribulation. But take courage; I have overcome the world!" (John 16:33). So your peace doesn't come from a trouble-free life, baker. It comes from Jesus, who has already won, and from the Spirit He sends to walk with you.
